title: Coral Filter (CORAL)
summary: Six chained exponential smoothings recombined with polynomial weights into a smooth trend line that lags less than a plain average.
descriptionHtml:
The Coral Filter runs the source through six exponential smoothing stages in a row, each one smoothing the output of the stage before it. The smoothing constant comes from the period: an effective length of (Period - 1) / 2 + 1, and a weight of 2 / (length + 1).

The result is not the last stage. It is a weighted sum of stages three to six, with weights that are polynomials in the Constant D setting: -d^3 on stage six, 3(d^2 + d^3) on stage five, -3(2d^2 + d + d^3) on stage four and 3d + 1 + d^3 + 3d^2 on stage three. The weights add up to 1, and they cancel much of the lag that six stages of smoothing would otherwise build up. Every stage starts at zero, so the line rises from zero on the first bars and settles onto price over the first few periods.
howToReadHtml:
Use it as a trend line. Price above a rising Coral line describes an uptrend and price below a falling one a downtrend, and a change in the slope of the line is a sign the trend is turning. Because the line is very smooth, its slope gives a cleaner read of direction than price itself.

A higher Constant D makes the line follow price more closely, with more wiggle; a lower one makes it smoother and slower. Ignore the first stretch of bars, where the line is still climbing from its zero start.

settings.label: Smoothing Period
settings.html: Sets the smoothing constant of all six stages. Longer is smoother and slower.

settings.label: Constant D
settings.html: Weights the stages against each other, from 0 to 1. Higher follows price more closely at the cost of smoothness.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series that is filtered, the close by default.

faq.q: Why does the line start near zero?
faq.html: All six stages are set to zero before the first bar, so the line needs a few periods to climb onto price. Read it once it has settled.
It sets how the four outer stages are mixed. Larger values give more weight to the faster stages and less lag; smaller values give a smoother, slower line.

related.title: Cubic Regression Moving Average (CRMA)
related.summary: Fits a cubic curve to the lookback window by least squares and plots the fitted value at the newest bar.

related.title: Convolution Moving Average (CONV)
related.summary: Weights the last few prices by a kernel of numbers you type in, so any smoother or filter can be written as a list of weights.

related.title: Ehlers Decycler (DECYCLER)
related.summary: Removes the cycles shorter than a cutoff period from price, leaving a trend line with very little lag.
